final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim to a caveated position based on the same record. That reframing improves precision, but it does not resolve the core compliance predicate. Under the provided policy text, a weakness is material if it affects a named launch use case, and low-volume or non-core characterizations do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending. The current record still lacks evidence of one of the required paths for a material weakness before launch: resolution, required disclosure, or approved risk acceptance. That means the Actor's position may be a more careful governance argument, but it is still not adequately supported as a compliance conclusion on the present record. The distinction matters: narrowing an overbroad claim can justify softer language, but it does not convert an unresolved policy condition into compliant_with_caveats when the caveat itself is the unresolved compliance requirement.
remaining_concerns: The affected segment is a named launch use case under the stated policy, which keeps materiality live despite the 7% traffic characterization.
The record still shows open legal review and no approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, not satisfaction of the disclosure/materiality predicate.
No admissible evidence shows the required before-launch disclosure, a final legal determination, or an approved exception path.
The Actor's caveated framing is narrower and more accurate, but it remains a reframing of the same evidence rather than proof that current certification is policy-compliant.
